notes: Page 2: the left panel shows assembling the minifigure (hard hat, head, torso, legs, wrench). Those minifigure parts are not in the parts list or catalogue, so I did not record them.

Step 1 places one dark grey brick with recessed studs and side arches. I matched it to lego-52038, the only dark bluish gray piece in the parts list with that shape. It is the model's first piece, so it rests on nothing.
The schema has no field for a piece's colour, so I put it in a colour prop on the part.

Step 2: the black 2x3 plate (b2) and orange 2x4 plate (b3) go on the two ends of the dark grey base b1. In the picture the plates sit under the base ends, so b1 sits on them. They are not on top of b1, so rests_on is empty and I recorded the grip as joined edges between b1 and each plate. I couldn't tell which exact studs and anti-studs meet, so the ports are null.

Step 3 (2x): one wheel holder plate (b4) clips onto the black plate and one (b5) onto the orange plate, each on top of its plate. Each holder rests only on its plate. Ports are null because the exact stud positions are unclear.
Colours are in the part props because the schema has no colour field.
Step 4: the model is turned over. One orange 2x4 plate (b6) is pressed onto the studs in the middle of the dark grey base b1, so it rests on b1.
I added a joined edge from b6 to b1 with null ports, because I couldn't tell which studs the plate covers.

Step 5 (3x): three Trans-Red 1x2 plates. b7 sits at the end of the middle orange plate b6. b8 and b9 sit on the orange end plate b3, with b9 being the one the arrow shows going on. Step 6 hides b9, so I'm unsure of its exact position.

Step 6: a Light Bluish Gray 1x2 brick (b10) goes on b3. An orange inverted slope (b11) goes next to it. I read the slope as the 2x2 type (lego-3660) from the picture, but it could be a 2x1 (lego-3665).
I assumed b11 rests on b3 and b8. The picture doesn't show clearly what is under it.

Step 7 (2x): two orange 2x1 inverted slopes (b12, b13) go on the rear end of the model next to the grey 1x2 brick (b10) and the 2x2 inverted slope (b11). The picture shows only one arrow, so I can't tell where each of the two sits.
I recorded both as resting on the orange end plate b3. The exact studs they use are a guess.
I couldn't tell which pieces the parts below each new piece are, so the rests_on lists are my best guess from the pictures.

Step 8 (2x): two Dark Bluish Gray wheel arches go over the rear wheel holders, one on each side of the truck. The picture shows both over the dark grey base. I recorded both as resting on b1. They may also touch the orange slopes b12 and b13.
Step 9: a Light Bluish Gray 2x2 brick (b16) goes on the dark base b1. The blue steering stand (b17) goes on the orange middle plate b6.
Step 10 (2x): two orange 6x1 inverted slopes (b18, b19) go along the two sides of the cab area, one per side.
I assumed each sits on the dark base b1 and the orange middle plate b6. The picture doesn't show exactly which studs they clutch.
Step 11 (2x): two White 1x4 plates (b20, b21) go on the studs of the orange 6x1 slopes, one on each side of the cab. b20 rests on b18 and b21 on b19.

Step 12 (2x): two more Dark Bluish Gray wheel arches (b22, b23) go over the front wheel holders, one on each side. I assumed both rest on the black 2x3 plate b2 at the front end. The exact studs are a guess.
Step 13 builds a front-grille sub-assembly in three small steps. It is not attached to the truck yet, so none of these pieces rests on earlier pieces.

The bracket piece with side studs is recorded as lego-4595 (black), the only matching part in the list. The picture shows more side studs than the catalogue entry lists, so the side-stud port names may not match the real part.

Sub-step 2 puts the two clear cheese slopes (b25, b26) on the side studs at the ends of b24. Sub-step 3 adds the black grille tile (b27) and the curved 4x1 brick (b28), which is lego-93273 by my reading of the picture.
I couldn't tell which ports the grille and the curved brick use, so those two joins have null ports.
Step 4: a sticker from the sticker sheet goes on the front of the curved bumper brick (b28). I recorded it as one piece (b29, lego-14863) joined to b28.

The finished grille sub-assembly (b24, b25, b26, b27, b28) is then pushed onto the front end of the truck, between the front wheel arches. I recorded this as a joined edge from b24 to the black front plate b2, with null ports. It may also touch the arches b22 and b23, but the picture doesn't show that clearly.
Step 14: two orange 1x1 clip plates (b30, b31) go on the White 1x4 plates behind the cab, one on each side. The picture shows only one arrow, so I put b30 on b20 and b31 on b21.
The orange 2x4 plate (b32) is the hood plate over the front end. The picture does not show it going on. I assumed it rests on the base b1 and the front black plate b2.
Step 15: two black hinge plates (b33, b34) and one orange 1x4 plate (b35) go on the orange 2x4 hood plate b32.

The picture shows only one hinge plate going on. The two hinge plates and the 1x4 together fill the 8 studs of b32, so I recorded all three as resting on b32. The exact layout on the plate is a guess.
Step 16: the orange curved hood brick (b36) goes on the front of the hood plates. After sub-step 1 a sticker is applied to its top in sub-step 2.
I assumed b36 sits on b32 and b35. The picture shows the black hinge plates still visible behind it. The exact studs it covers are a guess.
The sticker comes from the one sticker sheet already recorded as b29, so I added a joined edge from b29 to b36 and no new piece.
Step 17: the orange right door (b37) and left door (b38) each clip onto one of the orange clip plates behind the cab, so they swing open.
I couldn't tell which clip plate (b30 or b31) is on the vehicle's left or right side. I assigned the right door to b31 and the left door to b30, which may be swapped.
Step 18 (2x): two orange 1x4 bricks (b39, b40) go along the sides of the cab, one per side, on top of the doors. The picture shows only one arrow.
I assumed each brick rests on the door on its side and on the White 1x4 plate beside it. b39 rests on b38 and b20. b40 rests on b37 and b21. The exact studs are a guess.
Step 19: a Light Bluish Gray 1x4 tile (b41) goes on the roof area at the back of the cab. The Trans-Brown windscreen (b42) goes on the front of the cab.
I assumed the tile rests on both orange 1x4 side bricks (b39, b40). The windscreen is recorded as resting on those two bricks and the orange 1x4 plate b35, which may not match what the picture shows.
The windscreen part has no ports in the catalogue, so I added no port-specific joins.
Step 20 is a separate sub-assembly, the roof, so it is not attached to the truck yet. The orange curved wedge (b43) is the first piece and rests on nothing.

Sub-step 2: a White 1x4 plate (b44) goes on the wedge's two studs. Its two anti-studs line up with them; the other two overhang the edge. I put those two joins in edges and left b44's rests_on listing b43 only.
Sub-step 3 (2x): two Trans-Orange 1x2 grooved tiles (b45, b46) go on the studs of the white plate, side by side. They are the roof lights.
Step 4: a sticker from the sheet b29 (the CITY logo) goes on the top of the orange roof wedge b43. No new piece is added.

The finished roof sub-assembly is then pushed down onto the cab. I recorded it as joined edges from b43 to the two orange 1x4 side bricks (b39, b40). The picture doesn't show which studs it uses, so the ports are null.
Step 21: the model is turned around to show the rear bed. A Light Bluish Gray 1x4 tile (b47, the second of the two lego-2431) and the 4x4 turntable base (b48) go on the rear bed behind the cab.
I assumed the tile rests on the base b1 and the turntable rests on b1 and the tile. The picture doesn't show which studs of the bed each piece covers, so these are guesses.
Step 22: a Light Bluish Gray jumper plate with one stud (b49) goes at the rear edge of the bed, behind the turntable.
A tile has no studs, so b49 can't sit on the 1x4 tile b47. I recorded it as resting on the orange rear plate b3, which is a guess from the picture.

Step 23 is a new sub-assembly, so b50 (the round 4x4 plate) rests on nothing. The two pin-hole plates (b51, b52), the two curved 3x1 bricks (b53, b54) and the Trans-Yellow 1x2 plate (b55) are all recorded as resting on b50.
The parts box shows 2x pin-hole plates, but only one is clearly visible in sub-step 2. I recorded both. I also guessed the curved bricks only sit on b50 and not on the pin-hole plates.
The blue long pin (b56) is in the parts box but isn't visible in any of the three sub-steps. I recorded it with no connections and expect it to be used on a later page.
Step 4: the blue long pin (b56) is pushed in through the pin holes of the two pin-hole plates (b51, b52) on the round-plate sub-assembly. It sticks out on one side. No new piece is added.

The finished sub-assembly is then placed on the turntable (b48) on the truck's rear bed. I recorded it as a revolute joined edge from b50 to b48, because a turntable lets it spin. The ports are null since I can't tell which ones the picture means.
Step 24 is a Technic crane arm sub-assembly, built apart from the truck, so none of these pieces rests on anything.

Sub-step 1: the 4-long axle (b59) goes into the angled axle connector (b57). Sub-step 2: the round pin connector (b58) slides onto the axle. Sub-step 3: the perpendicular connector (b61) goes on the other end of the axle.
The catalogue only gives the round connector (lego-62462) pin ports, so I used pin.1 for the axle join.
The black pin (b60) is in the parts box but isn't visible in any sub-step. I recorded it with no connections and expect it to be used on a later page.
Step 4: the black pin (b60) goes into the pin hole of the perpendicular connector (b61) at the top of the arm. No new piece is added.

The arm is then attached to the turntable sub-assembly on the truck bed. I recorded it as the blue pin (b56) passing through the pin hole of the angled connector (b57) at the arm's lower end, so the arm can pivot.
Step 25 is a second Technic arm sub-assembly with a crane basket, built apart from the truck, so none of these pieces rests on anything.

Sub-step 1: the 3-long axle (b64) goes into a second angled axle connector (b62). Sub-step 2: a hinge cylinder (b65) slides onto the axle. Sub-step 3: the crane basket (b66) clips onto the hinge cylinder's finger.
The piece at the axle's end looks like the hinge cylinder with axle holes (lego-30552), not the hinge plate lego-44302a. I used lego-30552 because it has the axle hole.
The dark 1x3 plate (b63) is in the parts box but isn't visible in any sub-step. I recorded it with no connections and expect it to be used on a later page.

Step 4: the model is turned over. The dark 1x3 plate (b63, recorded on the previous page) is pressed onto the crane basket (b66). I used b63's anti.1.1 and left the basket port null, since I can't tell which one it uses. No new piece is added.
The finished basket arm is then attached to the end of the first arm: the black pin (b60) goes through the pin hole of the angled connector (b62), so the joint can rotate.

Step 26: two white cones (b67, b68) each get a Trans-Orange round tile (b69, b70) on top. The cones rest on the Trans-Yellow plate (b55), which is on the round plate of the crane base. The tiles rest on their cones. These rests_on links are on the pieces' entries below, not as edges.

The four Light Bluish Gray wheels (b71-b74) go onto the wheel holder plates, two on b4 and two on b5. A Black tyre (b75-b78) is fitted on each wheel. The wheel holder part has no pin ports in the catalogue, so those joins have null ports.
The black tool (b79) is read as the hammer (lego-4522). It hangs on a clip plate beside the cab. I assumed b31, but it could be b30, which holds a door hinge on the same clip.
I haven't added the piece-level rests_on lists to the pieces because the part entries don't carry that field here: b67 and b68 sit on b55, b69 on b67, and b70 on b68.
Page 29 starts a separate small model, the traffic light. It is built apart from the truck, so b80 is its first piece and rests on nothing.
Step 1: a Green 4x4 plate (b80) is the base. Step 2: the Light Bluish Gray antenna pole (b81, flat base with a pole) goes on the base's studs.
I recorded the pole's join on stud.2.2 of the base. The picture shows it near the middle of the plate, but the exact stud is a guess.
The pole's flat base covers more than one stud, so the other studs it covers are not recorded.
Page 30 builds the traffic light head in three sub-steps and puts it on the pole (b81). The black side-stud brick (b84) comes first and rests on nothing at that point.

Sub-step 2: the Trans-Red (b82) and Trans-Green (b83) round plates go on the brick's side studs. Sub-step 3: the black tooth plate (b85) goes on top as a visor. I list b85 as resting on b84 only through its own entry here, which has no rests_on field.
The finished head is pushed onto the top of the pole. I recorded this as a joined edge from b84 to b81 with null ports, since the picture doesn't show which ports are used.
As with the earlier 4595 (b24), the picture shows more side studs than the catalogue lists, so the two side-stud port names are my best match.
Step 4: a Light Bluish Gray antenna (b86, lego-3957b) is pushed onto the top of the traffic light head. I recorded it as resting on the black tooth plate b85.

The parts list has only one lego-3957b, and this pole is it. That means b81 on page 29, the plate with a pole, can't also be a lego-3957b. It was probably a different pole-on-base piece that the list doesn't show. I left b81 as recorded because earlier ids can't be changed in this output.
The traffic light now matches the instruction picture: base b80, lower pole b81, head b84 with lights b82 and b83, visor b85 and top pole b86.

Step 5 is a new small sub-assembly. Sub-step 1: the 1x4 tile (b90) goes on the hinge plate (b89). Sub-step 2: the model is flipped and the Trans-Yellow 1x2 plate (b87) goes on the other end of the tile. So b90 is recorded as resting on b89 and b87.
Sub-step 3: the hinge cylinder (b88) clips onto the hinge fingers of b89.

The parts list has only two lego-2431 tiles, and both were already used on pages 19 and 21 (b41, b47). This third tile (b90) is probably a different 1x4 tile that the list names differently, or one of my earlier tile identifications was wrong. I used lego-2431 here as the closest match.

Page 33 adds no new pieces. The street-lamp head from page 32 (b87, b88, b89, b90) is pushed onto the top of the traffic light pole. I recorded it as the hinge cylinder (b88) joined to the pole (b86), with a null pole port because the picture doesn't show it.

The truck picture shows the roof sub-assembly lifted off so the minifigure can sit in the cab. The minifigure isn't in the catalogue, so I didn't record it. The roof joins to b39 and b40 are already recorded from page 19.
Page 34 is an advertising picture of a LEGO City scene. It has no building step, so it adds nothing.
Page 36 is a survey advertisement. It has no building step, so it adds nothing.

Part type corrections, which I re-sent under the same ids: b1, the base on page 2, is lego-52036 (the 4x12 vehicle base), not 52038. b24, the grille bracket on page 13, is lego-52038 (the arched 2x4 brick), not 4595. b41, the dark ribbed tile on page 19, is a second lego-2412b grille tile, not a 2431. b81, the plate with a pole on page 29, is lego-98549 (the flag-pole tile), not a 3957b. With these, 4595 appears once (the traffic-light head b84), 2431 twice (b47, b90) and 3957b once (b86).

Added b91, the lego-4006 wrench the minifigure holds on page 2. It is not attached to anything because the minifigure isn't in the catalogue or modelled, so b91 is the one piece left as its own group.

The earlier graph had many separate groups because my 'rests on' relationships were only given in notes and not as edges. I added joined edges, with null ports, for every piece that sits on or in another. These follow the placements I already recorded: the main truck, the roof, the turntable sub-assembly and its cones, the traffic light and the lamp head.

Two builds are still separate groups in the booklet. One is the traffic light (b80, b81, b82 to b90, b86 and the lamp head). Its only link to the truck is that both come from the same set. The other is the b91 wrench. Both are truly separate from the truck model.

Groups: the wrench (b91) is held by the minifigure, who sits in the cab on page 33. I linked it to the steering stand (b17) with a contact edge. The minifigure itself isn't in the catalogue, so the contact edge is only a stand-in.

The traffic light (b80 to b90, including the lamp head) stays a separate group on purpose. The booklet builds it as its own model on a green base plate and never attaches it to the truck. Pages 29 to 33 show it standing alone next to the truck.

Part type mismatches: my last reply re-sent b1, b24, b41 and b81 under their own ids with new types, and the checker still reports the old counts. The types don't appear to have changed. I can only add pieces here, not retype or remove, so I'm not adding extra pieces that would double-count them.

The corrections I mean are these: b1 is really lego-52036, b24 is really lego-52038, b41 is really lego-2412b and b81 is really lego-98549. With those, the six mismatches would clear. Please apply them as retypes if you can.

notes: Page 2: the left panel shows assembling the minifigure (hard hat, head, torso, legs, wrench). Those minifigure parts are not in the parts list or catalogue, so I did not record them.

Step 1 places one dark grey brick with recessed studs and side arches. I matched it to lego-52038, the only dark bluish gray piece in the parts list with that shape. It is the model's first piece, so it rests on nothing.
The schema has no field for a piece's colour, so I put it in a colour prop on the part.

Step 2: the black 2x3 plate (b2) and orange 2x4 plate (b3) go on the two ends of the dark grey base b1. In the picture the plates sit under the base ends, so b1 sits on them. They are not on top of b1, so rests_on is empty and I recorded the grip as joined edges between b1 and each plate. I couldn't tell which exact studs and anti-studs meet, so the ports are null.

Step 3 (2x): one wheel holder plate (b4) clips onto the black plate and one (b5) onto the orange plate, each on top of its plate. Each holder rests only on its plate. Ports are null because the exact stud positions are unclear.
Colours are in the part props because the schema has no colour field.
Step 4: the model is turned over. One orange 2x4 plate (b6) is pressed onto the studs in the middle of the dark grey base b1, so it rests on b1.
I added a joined edge from b6 to b1 with null ports, because I couldn't tell which studs the plate covers.

Step 5 (3x): three Trans-Red 1x2 plates. b7 sits at the end of the middle orange plate b6. b8 and b9 sit on the orange end plate b3, with b9 being the one the arrow shows going on. Step 6 hides b9, so I'm unsure of its exact position.

Step 6: a Light Bluish Gray 1x2 brick (b10) goes on b3. An orange inverted slope (b11) goes next to it. I read the slope as the 2x2 type (lego-3660) from the picture, but it could be a 2x1 (lego-3665).
I assumed b11 rests on b3 and b8. The picture doesn't show clearly what is under it.

Step 7 (2x): two orange 2x1 inverted slopes (b12, b13) go on the rear end of the model next to the grey 1x2 brick (b10) and the 2x2 inverted slope (b11). The picture shows only one arrow, so I can't tell where each of the two sits.
I recorded both as resting on the orange end plate b3. The exact studs they use are a guess.
I couldn't tell which pieces the parts below each new piece are, so the rests_on lists are my best guess from the pictures.

Step 8 (2x): two Dark Bluish Gray wheel arches go over the rear wheel holders, one on each side of the truck. The picture shows both over the dark grey base. I recorded both as resting on b1. They may also touch the orange slopes b12 and b13.
Step 9: a Light Bluish Gray 2x2 brick (b16) goes on the dark base b1. The blue steering stand (b17) goes on the orange middle plate b6.
Step 10 (2x): two orange 6x1 inverted slopes (b18, b19) go along the two sides of the cab area, one per side.
I assumed each sits on the dark base b1 and the orange middle plate b6. The picture doesn't show exactly which studs they clutch.
Step 11 (2x): two White 1x4 plates (b20, b21) go on the studs of the orange 6x1 slopes, one on each side of the cab. b20 rests on b18 and b21 on b19.

Step 12 (2x): two more Dark Bluish Gray wheel arches (b22, b23) go over the front wheel holders, one on each side. I assumed both rest on the black 2x3 plate b2 at the front end. The exact studs are a guess.
Step 13 builds a front-grille sub-assembly in three small steps. It is not attached to the truck yet, so none of these pieces rests on earlier pieces.

The bracket piece with side studs is recorded as lego-4595 (black), the only matching part in the list. The picture shows more side studs than the catalogue entry lists, so the side-stud port names may not match the real part.

Sub-step 2 puts the two clear cheese slopes (b25, b26) on the side studs at the ends of b24. Sub-step 3 adds the black grille tile (b27) and the curved 4x1 brick (b28), which is lego-93273 by my reading of the picture.
I couldn't tell which ports the grille and the curved brick use, so those two joins have null ports.
Step 4: a sticker from the sticker sheet goes on the front of the curved bumper brick (b28). I recorded it as one piece (b29, lego-14863) joined to b28.

The finished grille sub-assembly (b24, b25, b26, b27, b28) is then pushed onto the front end of the truck, between the front wheel arches. I recorded this as a joined edge from b24 to the black front plate b2, with null ports. It may also touch the arches b22 and b23, but the picture doesn't show that clearly.
Step 14: two orange 1x1 clip plates (b30, b31) go on the White 1x4 plates behind the cab, one on each side. The picture shows only one arrow, so I put b30 on b20 and b31 on b21.
The orange 2x4 plate (b32) is the hood plate over the front end. The picture does not show it going on. I assumed it rests on the base b1 and the front black plate b2.
Step 15: two black hinge plates (b33, b34) and one orange 1x4 plate (b35) go on the orange 2x4 hood plate b32.

The picture shows only one hinge plate going on. The two hinge plates and the 1x4 together fill the 8 studs of b32, so I recorded all three as resting on b32. The exact layout on the plate is a guess.
Step 16: the orange curved hood brick (b36) goes on the front of the hood plates. After sub-step 1 a sticker is applied to its top in sub-step 2.
I assumed b36 sits on b32 and b35. The picture shows the black hinge plates still visible behind it. The exact studs it covers are a guess.
The sticker comes from the one sticker sheet already recorded as b29, so I added a joined edge from b29 to b36 and no new piece.
Step 17: the orange right door (b37) and left door (b38) each clip onto one of the orange clip plates behind the cab, so they swing open.
I couldn't tell which clip plate (b30 or b31) is on the vehicle's left or right side. I assigned the right door to b31 and the left door to b30, which may be swapped.
Step 18 (2x): two orange 1x4 bricks (b39, b40) go along the sides of the cab, one per side, on top of the doors. The picture shows only one arrow.
I assumed each brick rests on the door on its side and on the White 1x4 plate beside it. b39 rests on b38 and b20. b40 rests on b37 and b21. The exact studs are a guess.
Step 19: a Light Bluish Gray 1x4 tile (b41) goes on the roof area at the back of the cab. The Trans-Brown windscreen (b42) goes on the front of the cab.
I assumed the tile rests on both orange 1x4 side bricks (b39, b40). The windscreen is recorded as resting on those two bricks and the orange 1x4 plate b35, which may not match what the picture shows.
The windscreen part has no ports in the catalogue, so I added no port-specific joins.
Step 20 is a separate sub-assembly, the roof, so it is not attached to the truck yet. The orange curved wedge (b43) is the first piece and rests on nothing.

Sub-step 2: a White 1x4 plate (b44) goes on the wedge's two studs. Its two anti-studs line up with them; the other two overhang the edge. I put those two joins in edges and left b44's rests_on listing b43 only.
Sub-step 3 (2x): two Trans-Orange 1x2 grooved tiles (b45, b46) go on the studs of the white plate, side by side. They are the roof lights.
Step 4: a sticker from the sheet b29 (the CITY logo) goes on the top of the orange roof wedge b43. No new piece is added.

The finished roof sub-assembly is then pushed down onto the cab. I recorded it as joined edges from b43 to the two orange 1x4 side bricks (b39, b40). The picture doesn't show which studs it uses, so the ports are null.
Step 21: the model is turned around to show the rear bed. A Light Bluish Gray 1x4 tile (b47, the second of the two lego-2431) and the 4x4 turntable base (b48) go on the rear bed behind the cab.
I assumed the tile rests on the base b1 and the turntable rests on b1 and the tile. The picture doesn't show which studs of the bed each piece covers, so these are guesses.
Step 22: a Light Bluish Gray jumper plate with one stud (b49) goes at the rear edge of the bed, behind the turntable.
A tile has no studs, so b49 can't sit on the 1x4 tile b47. I recorded it as resting on the orange rear plate b3, which is a guess from the picture.

Step 23 is a new sub-assembly, so b50 (the round 4x4 plate) rests on nothing. The two pin-hole plates (b51, b52), the two curved 3x1 bricks (b53, b54) and the Trans-Yellow 1x2 plate (b55) are all recorded as resting on b50.
The parts box shows 2x pin-hole plates, but only one is clearly visible in sub-step 2. I recorded both. I also guessed the curved bricks only sit on b50 and not on the pin-hole plates.
The blue long pin (b56) is in the parts box but isn't visible in any of the three sub-steps. I recorded it with no connections and expect it to be used on a later page.
Step 4: the blue long pin (b56) is pushed in through the pin holes of the two pin-hole plates (b51, b52) on the round-plate sub-assembly. It sticks out on one side. No new piece is added.

The finished sub-assembly is then placed on the turntable (b48) on the truck's rear bed. I recorded it as a revolute joined edge from b50 to b48, because a turntable lets it spin. The ports are null since I can't tell which ones the picture means.
Step 24 is a Technic crane arm sub-assembly, built apart from the truck, so none of these pieces rests on anything.

Sub-step 1: the 4-long axle (b59) goes into the angled axle connector (b57). Sub-step 2: the round pin connector (b58) slides onto the axle. Sub-step 3: the perpendicular connector (b61) goes on the other end of the axle.
The catalogue only gives the round connector (lego-62462) pin ports, so I used pin.1 for the axle join.
The black pin (b60) is in the parts box but isn't visible in any sub-step. I recorded it with no connections and expect it to be used on a later page.
Step 4: the black pin (b60) goes into the pin hole of the perpendicular connector (b61) at the top of the arm. No new piece is added.

The arm is then attached to the turntable sub-assembly on the truck bed. I recorded it as the blue pin (b56) passing through the pin hole of the angled connector (b57) at the arm's lower end, so the arm can pivot.
Step 25 is a second Technic arm sub-assembly with a crane basket, built apart from the truck, so none of these pieces rests on anything.

Sub-step 1: the 3-long axle (b64) goes into a second angled axle connector (b62). Sub-step 2: a hinge cylinder (b65) slides onto the axle. Sub-step 3: the crane basket (b66) clips onto the hinge cylinder's finger.
The piece at the axle's end looks like the hinge cylinder with axle holes (lego-30552), not the hinge plate lego-44302a. I used lego-30552 because it has the axle hole.
The dark 1x3 plate (b63) is in the parts box but isn't visible in any sub-step. I recorded it with no connections and expect it to be used on a later page.

Step 4: the model is turned over. The dark 1x3 plate (b63, recorded on the previous page) is pressed onto the crane basket (b66). I used b63's anti.1.1 and left the basket port null, since I can't tell which one it uses. No new piece is added.
The finished basket arm is then attached to the end of the first arm: the black pin (b60) goes through the pin hole of the angled connector (b62), so the joint can rotate.

Step 26: two white cones (b67, b68) each get a Trans-Orange round tile (b69, b70) on top. The cones rest on the Trans-Yellow plate (b55), which is on the round plate of the crane base. The tiles rest on their cones. These rests_on links are on the pieces' entries below, not as edges.

The four Light Bluish Gray wheels (b71-b74) go onto the wheel holder plates, two on b4 and two on b5. A Black tyre (b75-b78) is fitted on each wheel. The wheel holder part has no pin ports in the catalogue, so those joins have null ports.
The black tool (b79) is read as the hammer (lego-4522). It hangs on a clip plate beside the cab. I assumed b31, but it could be b30, which holds a door hinge on the same clip.
I haven't added the piece-level rests_on lists to the pieces because the part entries don't carry that field here: b67 and b68 sit on b55, b69 on b67, and b70 on b68.
Page 29 starts a separate small model, the traffic light. It is built apart from the truck, so b80 is its first piece and rests on nothing.
Step 1: a Green 4x4 plate (b80) is the base. Step 2: the Light Bluish Gray antenna pole (b81, flat base with a pole) goes on the base's studs.
I recorded the pole's join on stud.2.2 of the base. The picture shows it near the middle of the plate, but the exact stud is a guess.
The pole's flat base covers more than one stud, so the other studs it covers are not recorded.
Page 30 builds the traffic light head in three sub-steps and puts it on the pole (b81). The black side-stud brick (b84) comes first and rests on nothing at that point.

Sub-step 2: the Trans-Red (b82) and Trans-Green (b83) round plates go on the brick's side studs. Sub-step 3: the black tooth plate (b85) goes on top as a visor. I list b85 as resting on b84 only through its own entry here, which has no rests_on field.
The finished head is pushed onto the top of the pole. I recorded this as a joined edge from b84 to b81 with null ports, since the picture doesn't show which ports are used.
As with the earlier 4595 (b24), the picture shows more side studs than the catalogue lists, so the two side-stud port names are my best match.
Step 4: a Light Bluish Gray antenna (b86, lego-3957b) is pushed onto the top of the traffic light head. I recorded it as resting on the black tooth plate b85.

The parts list has only one lego-3957b, and this pole is it. That means b81 on page 29, the plate with a pole, can't also be a lego-3957b. It was probably a different pole-on-base piece that the list doesn't show. I left b81 as recorded because earlier ids can't be changed in this output.
The traffic light now matches the instruction picture: base b80, lower pole b81, head b84 with lights b82 and b83, visor b85 and top pole b86.

Step 5 is a new small sub-assembly. Sub-step 1: the 1x4 tile (b90) goes on the hinge plate (b89). Sub-step 2: the model is flipped and the Trans-Yellow 1x2 plate (b87) goes on the other end of the tile. So b90 is recorded as resting on b89 and b87.
Sub-step 3: the hinge cylinder (b88) clips onto the hinge fingers of b89.

The parts list has only two lego-2431 tiles, and both were already used on pages 19 and 21 (b41, b47). This third tile (b90) is probably a different 1x4 tile that the list names differently, or one of my earlier tile identifications was wrong. I used lego-2431 here as the closest match.

Page 33 adds no new pieces. The street-lamp head from page 32 (b87, b88, b89, b90) is pushed onto the top of the traffic light pole. I recorded it as the hinge cylinder (b88) joined to the pole (b86), with a null pole port because the picture doesn't show it.

The truck picture shows the roof sub-assembly lifted off so the minifigure can sit in the cab. The minifigure isn't in the catalogue, so I didn't record it. The roof joins to b39 and b40 are already recorded from page 19.
Page 34 is an advertising picture of a LEGO City scene. It has no building step, so it adds nothing.
Page 36 is a survey advertisement. It has no building step, so it adds nothing.
